name: gmssl
desc: Toolkit for Chinese national cryptographic standards
why: An open toolkit for Chinese national cryptographic standards like SM2, SM3 and SM4 is a rare window onto a different crypto world.

brief.what_it_is: GmSSL is an open-source cryptography library and command-line toolkit, written in C and built with CMake, that implements the Chinese national commercial cryptography standards: SM2, SM3, SM4, SM9 and ZUC. The README is in Chinese and says it was developed independently at Peking University. It also covers TLCP (GB/T 38636-2020), TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 with the RFC 8998 SM4-GCM-SM3 suite, X.509 certificates, CRLs, CSRs, PEM/PKCS #8 keys, SM2 digital envelopes, and some post-quantum signature schemes. Inputs are data, keys, certificates and protocol traffic; outputs are ciphertexts, digests, signatures, certificates and TLS sessions, through a `gmssl` CLI or a C library (libgmssl). Language bindings are provided as separate sub-projects.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says GmSSL is a domestic commercial cryptography library that gives full coverage of the national (GM/guomi) algorithms, standards and secure communication protocols, and that it is meant to make it easier to build products that must pass Chinese cryptographic product certification. It also supports Chinese cryptographic hardware (SDF PCI-E cards and servers, SKF USB keys).
brief.how_it_works: The library is organised around the national algorithms and protocols, with the TLS stack written as a state machine that supports non-blocking mode. GmSSL 3 can be configured to include only the national algorithms and the TLCP protocol, and it avoids dynamic memory allocation so it can run on bare-metal MCUs and SoCs. Hardware keys are reached through SDF or SKF interfaces, and the SoftSDF sub-project offers a software SDF module for development and testing.

commands_seen.context: Create a build directory inside the unpacked source tree (Unix build steps).
Enter the build directory before running CMake.
Configure the build from the parent source directory; add -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF to get libgmssl.a instead of a shared library.
Install the gmssl CLI, the gmssl header directory and libgmssl.so or libgmssl.dylib into system locations.
Configure a Windows build from a Visual Studio command prompt.
Build on Windows after the NMake configuration step.
Configure with speed tests enabled, for benchmarking.
Run the benchmark binaries for SM4, SM3, SM2, SM9 and ZUC after the speed-test build.

brief.install_notes: Standard CMake build: mkdir build, cmake .., make, make test, sudo make install. The build no longer depends on Perl. Windows uses Visual Studio with the NMake generator and -DWIN32=ON. Android NDK, iOS and OpenHarmony builds are covered by CI badges in the README. Hardware support is optional: SDF and SKF devices, or SoftSDF as a software stand-in. No accounts or runtimes are mentioned.
brief.standout: Few open-source libraries cover the Chinese national crypto suite (SM2/SM3/SM4/SM9/ZUC plus TLCP and the RFC 8998 TLS 1.3 suite) as a complete, cross-platform package with a CLI. The OpenSSL-Compatibility-Layer lets Nginx 1.16 to 1.25 run on GmSSL, and the README says it has been tested with those versions.
brief.status: unknown. The README names GmSSL-3.2.0 as the current stable release and has a ChangeLog that runs from 3.1.1 onward, with CI badges for several platforms. It gives no release date or last-commit date, so the README alone cannot confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: The README is in Chinese; this brief is based on a translation of the key points. The hardware-tested list is an unfinished placeholder ('to be added'). GmSSL 3 is not API- or drop-in compatible with OpenSSL, and the compatibility layer is limited to the tested Nginx range. Benchmark numbers are the author's own, on Apple M2 and a 2018 Intel MacBook Pro. Licence is not stated in the README I read. The README gives no usage examples for the gmssl CLI itself.
quotes: 超轻量：GmSSL 3 大幅度降低了内存需求和二进制代码体积，不依赖动态内存，可以用于无操作系统的低功耗嵌入式环境(MCU、SOC等)
更合规：GmSSL 3 可以配置为仅包含国密算法和国密协议(TLCP协议)

judge.reason: A rare, hands-on window into China’s cryptographic standards, from SM algorithms to TLCP and hardware-backed keys, rather than just another general-purpose crypto library.

entry.title: GmSSL
entry.tldr: A C crypto library and gmssl command-line tool implementing China's national cryptography standards (SM2, SM3, SM4, SM9, ZUC), a different crypto lineage from the usual AES and RSA.
entry.deeper_look:
GmSSL is an open-source cryptography toolkit written in C. It implements the Chinese national commercial cryptography algorithms, often called guomi or GM: SM2 for public-key work, SM3 for hashing, SM4 for block encryption, SM9 for identity-based crypto, and ZUC for stream encryption. It also covers X.509 certificates, CSRs, CRLs, PEM and PKCS #8 keys, SM2 digital envelopes, and some post-quantum signature schemes. You reach it through a `gmssl` command-line tool or the libgmssl C library.

It also speaks the protocols built on those algorithms: TLCP (GB/T 38636-2020), TLS 1.2, and TLS 1.3 with the RFC 8998 SM4-GCM-SM3 suite. The README says the project exists so that products can pass Chinese cryptographic product certification. It supports Chinese crypto hardware too, namely SDF PCI-E cards and servers and SKF USB keys. A SoftSDF sub-project provides a software stand-in for development.

The idea underneath is that cryptography is also standardised nationally, and the algorithms most Western developers know are one lineage among several. GmSSL lets you hash, sign and encrypt with the other one and compare how it is put together. Version 3 was rewritten from scratch. It can be configured to include only the national algorithms, avoids dynamic memory allocation, and is meant to run on bare-metal microcontrollers. Its TLS stack is a state machine that supports non-blocking mode.

try_this.what_happens: Lists the subcommands the CLI offers, a starting map of the SM algorithms and certificate tools it exposes.

entry.whats_unique: Few open-source libraries cover the whole Chinese national suite, including TLCP and the RFC 8998 TLS 1.3 suite, as a cross-platform package with a CLI. An OpenSSL compatibility layer lets Nginx 1.16 to 1.25 run on it.
entry.caveats: The README is in Chinese and gives no CLI usage examples, so expect to explore with --help; GmSSL 3 is not API-compatible with OpenSSL, and recent activity could not be confirmed from the README.
